result:
Both checks pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` reports 16 pass / 0 fail (the 5 pre-existing tests plus 11 new ones).

I added `app/Http/SafeRedirect.ts`, holding the default post-login destination (`DEFAULT_REDIRECT = '/dashboard'`) and a `safeRedirectPath(value, fallback)` helper that reduces a client-supplied redirect to a path inside the app: it first removes the tabs/newlines browsers strip from a URL before resolving it, trims, and then keeps the value only if it starts with a single `/`, contains no backslash (the `/\evil.example` spelling browsers normalise into `//evil.example`), and carries no control characters — everything else, including absolute URLs, other schemes, and protocol-relative values, falls back. `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.ts` now runs both redirect sources through it: `show()` sanitizes `?redirect=` with an empty fallback so the login form's hidden field can never carry an off-site value back, and `store()` sanitizes the body value (with the query string as fallback, as before) against `DEFAULT_REDIRECT` right before `this.redirect()`, leaving credential checking untouched. I noted the sanitization in the `redirect` field comment in `app/Http/Validators/LoginValidator.ts`, and added `tests/SafeRedirect.test.ts` (unit coverage of the accepted and rejected shapes) plus `tests/LoginController.test.ts` (HTTP coverage: the login page keeps `/posts/3/edit` and drops `https://evil.example` from its props; a correct password redirects to `/posts/3/edit`, while absolute, protocol-relative, backslash, and query-string off-site values all sign in and land on `/dashboard`; a wrong password still returns 422 with no redirect).
